predecessors.name: Nazca culture
predecessors.text: the Nasca coast, 'a city believed to have been under heavy Wari influence' (Huari page)

ledger.x: c. 600: the Wari state emerges at Huari in the Ayacucho Basin. 'Emerged in around 600 CE'; infobox 'Established: 6th century', capital Huari; the Huari page: the city 'founded ca. 400 AD and gained prominence around 550 AD', about 70,000 inhabitants, 2,000 ha.
The Wari expand in the seventh century.
The Nasca coast falls under the Wari.

c. 1000: the Wari state ends. 'The city was abandoned ca. 1000 AD'; 'the Wari culture ... lasted from 600-1000'. The Wari Empire page says the polity 'seems to have survived until ca. AD 1100' (infobox 'Disestablished: 11th century') and that decline began in the 10th century.

wars.name: Wari-Tiwanaku rivalry
wars.outcome: No war recorded: the two 'coexisted at Moquegua without conflict'; Joyce Marcus compares their rivalry to the Cold War.

certainty.note: No limits on either page; the provincial centres are points.
